The cuckoo clock had just struck five, and he was aware that he was, at this very moment, for the first time in his life, eight years old. He had gone to bed at eight o'clock on the preceding evening with the choking consciousness that he would awake in the morning a different creature.

arxiv-1912-13077.title: Learning Selective Sensor Fusion for States Estimation
arxiv-1912-13077.creator: Changhao Chen*, Stefano Rosa, Chris Xiaoxuan Lu, Bing Wang, Niki Trigoni, Andrew Markham
arxiv-1912-13077.description: Abstract Autonomous vehicles and mobile robotic systems are typically equipped with multiple sensors to provide redundancy. By integrating the observations from different sensors, these mobile agents are able to perceive the environment and estimate system states, e.g. locations and orientations.

arxiv-2206-02276.title: Restricted Birkhoff polytopes and Ehrhart period collapse
arxiv-2206-02276.creator: Per Alexandersson, Sam Hopkins, Gjergji Zaimi
arxiv-2206-02276.description: Abstract . We show that the polytopes obtained from the Birkhoff polytope by imposing additional inequalities restricting the “longest increasing subsequence” have Ehrhart quasi-polynomials which are honest polynomials, even though they are just rational polytopes in general. We do this by defining a continuous, piecewise-linear bijection to a certain Gelfand–Tsetlin polytope.

arxiv-2304-11914.title: Investigating the impact of extra resonance states in the van der Waals Hadron Resonance Gas Model
arxiv-2304-11914.creator: Nachiketa Sarkar
arxiv-2304-11914.description: Abstract We investigate, in addition to the experimentally established hadrons, how the inclusion of extra resonance states, through the Hagedorn mass spectrum (HS) or Quark Model (QM) predicated states, affects the thermodynamic and transport quantities of the hadronic system in the van der Waals hadron resonance gas (VDWHRG) model.

arxiv-2401-13662.title: The Definitive Guide to Policy Gradients in Deep Reinforcement Learning: Theory, Algorithms and Implementations
arxiv-2401-13662.creator: Matthias Lehmann
arxiv-2401-13662.description: Abstract In recent years, various powerful policy gradient algorithms have been proposed in deep reinforcement learning. While all these algorithms build on the Policy Gradient Theorem, the specific design choices differ significantly across algorithms. We provide a holistic overview of on-policy policy gradient algorithms to facilitate the understanding of both their theoretical foundations and their practical implementations.

arxiv-2503-17724.title: Trigger without Trace: Towards Stealthy Backdoor Attack on Text-to-Image Diffusion Models Thanks: Jie Zhang, Zhongqi Wang, Shiguang Shan and Xilin Chen are with the Key Laboratory of AI Safety of CAS, Institute of Computing Technology (ICT), Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), Beijing 100190, China,
arxiv-2503-17724.creator: Jie Zhang, Zhongqi Wang
arxiv-2503-17724.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jie Zhang, Zhongqi Wang. Backdoor attacks targeting text-to-image diffusion models have advanced rapidly. However, current backdoor samples often exhibit two key abnormalities compared to benign samples: 1) Semantic Consistency , where backdoor prompts tend to generate images with similar semantic content even with significant textual variations to the prompts; 2) Attention Consistency , where the trigger induces consistent structural responses in the cross-attention maps. These consistencies leave detectable traces for defenders, making backdoors easier to identify.

arxiv-2507-06797.title: Unlocking Thermal Aerial Imaging: Synthetic Enhancement of UAV Datasets
arxiv-2507-06797.creator: Antonella Barisic Kulas, Andreja Jurasovic, Stjepan Bogdan
arxiv-2507-06797.description: Abstract Thermal imaging from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) holds significant potential for applications in search and rescue, wildlife monitoring, and emergency response, especially under low-light or obscured conditions. However, the scarcity of large-scale, diverse thermal aerial datasets limits the advancement of deep learning models in this domain, primarily due to the high cost and logistical challenges of collecting thermal data.

arxiv-2510-07822.title: SIMU: Selective Influence Machine Unlearning
arxiv-2510-07822.creator: Anu Agarwal, Mihir Pamnani, Dilek Hakkani-Tur
arxiv-2510-07822.description: Abstract The undesired memorization of sensitive information by Large Language Models (LLMs) has emphasized the need for safety mechanisms that can regulate model behavior. This has led to the development of machine unlearning techniques that enable models to precisely forget sensitive and unwanted information.

pmc-10552216.title: The effect of telephone counseling based on Orem’s model on adherence to treatment and resilience of patients with coronary angioplasty: a randomized clinical trial
pmc-10552216.creator: Khatereh Rostami, Mahsa Maryami, Masoume Rambod
pmc-10552216.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to determine the effect of telephone counseling based on Orem’s Self-Care Model on adherence to treatment and resilience of patients with coronary angioplasty.MethodsThis randomized clinical trial was performed on 80 patients in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit of Shiraz University of Medical Sciences. Patients were randomly divided into two groups of 40 (intervention and control).

pmc-10735437.title: NEIGHBORHOOD CHARACTERISTICS AND INEQUALITIES IN SENSORY HEALTH AMONG OLDER ADULTS IN THE UNITED STATES
pmc-10735437.creator: Alyssa Goldman, Jayant Pinto
pmc-10735437.description: Sensory function plays a crucial role in older adults’ navigation of the environment, maintenance of personal safety, and in quality of everyday life. The residential neighborhood context is a significant social determinant of later life health and health disparities, but it has been understudied with respect to sensory function.

pmc-11487829.title: Developing the ‘Life Threads’ approach to support families after traumatic brain injury in UK community settings: protocol for a qualitative prefeasibility study
pmc-11487829.creator: Charlotte Jane Whiffin, Caroline Ellis-Hill, Alyson Norman, Morag Lee, Parmjeet Kaur Singh, Jo Clark-Wilson, Audrey Daisley, Natasha Yasmin Felles, Mark Holloway, Sara Rose, Fergus Gracey
pmc-11487829.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionTraumatic brain injury (TBI) brings about inevitable and significant changes for family members. Mental health effects for family members are well documented but there are significant gaps in support options across services.

pmc-11632944.title: Complete chloroplast genome sequence of the medicinal plant Oxyceros horridus (Rubiaceae) and phylogenetic analysis
pmc-11632944.creator: Thu Thao Thi Huynh, Minh Trong Quang, Hoang Danh Nguyen
pmc-11632944.description: Oxyceros horridus Lour. 1790, valued for ornamental and medicinal properties, has been extensively utilized in traditional medicinal in Vietnam. This study assembled and characterized the first chloroplast of Oxyceros horridus, consisted of 155,333 bp with a GC content of 37.5%.

pmc-11713322.title: Human iPSC‐derived neuron modeling for the study of early‐onset Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11713322.creator: Phoebe Valdes, Andrew B Caldwell, Qing Liu, Kenneth W Henry, Michael Q Fitzgerald, Koushik Muralidharan, Srinivasan Ramachandran, Celeste M Karch, Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN), Shauna H Yuan, Steven L Wagner, Lawrence SB Goldstein, William C Mobley, Douglas R Galasko, Shankar Subram
pmc-11713322.description: BackgroundEarly‐onset Alzheimer’s disease (EOAD) is a complex disease that occurs at an early age at onset (AAO) before 65 years, constituting 5‐6% of all AD cases and remains poorly understood. Patient‐derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have been used to model different forms of EOAD that display heterogeneous disease mechanisms.

pmc-12385447.title: Is There a Role for the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio for Rebleeding and Mortality Risk Prediction in Acute Variceal Bleeding? A Comparative 5-Year Retrospective Study
pmc-12385447.creator: Sergiu Marian Cazacu, Dragos Ovidiu Alexandru, Alexandru Valentin Popescu, Petrica Popa, Ion Rogoveanu, Vlad Florin Iovanescu
pmc-12385447.description: (1) Background: Acute variceal bleeding (AVB) represents an important cause of upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB). Several prognostic scores may be useful for assessing mortality and rebleeding risk, with the Glasgow-Blatchford score (GBS) and Rockall score being the most commonly used for non-variceal bleeding. Scores assessing liver failure (MELD and Child) do not reflect bleeding severity.

pmc-12490163.title: Evaluating urine volume and host depletion methods to enable genome-resolved metagenomics of the urobiome
pmc-12490163.creator: Zachary J. Lewis, Angela Scott, Christopher Madden, Dean Vik, Ahmed A. Zayed, Garrett J. Smith, Sheryl S. Justice, Adam Rudinsky, Jessica Hokamp, Vanessa L. Hale
pmc-12490163.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe gut microbiome has emerged as a clear player in health and disease, in part by mediating host response to environment and lifestyle. The urobiome (microbiota of the urinary tract) likely functions similarly. However, efforts to characterize the urobiome and assess its functional potential have been limited due to technical challenges including low microbial biomass and high host cell shedding in urine.

pmc-12649130.title: Redox Control in Platelet Activity and Therapy
pmc-12649130.creator: Laura M. Dionisio, Yi Zheng, Jose A. Cancelas
pmc-12649130.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Maintaining redox balance is essential for platelet physiology and overall cellular homeostasis. Upon activation, platelets generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), which act as signaling mediators in responses to collagen and are required for collagen-dependent thrombus formation. Multiple enzymatic systems contribute to platelet ROS production, with nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (phosphate) oxidases (NOX isoforms) serving as the primary source, complemented by cyclooxygenase (COX), xanthine oxidase (XO), and the mitochondrial respiratory chain.

pmc-13286624.title: Perforated Necrotizing Cholecystitis, Niemeier Type II, With Subcutaneous Abscess in a Frail Elderly Patient: Challenges in Diagnosis and Management
pmc-13286624.creator: Michail Angelos Papaoikonomou, Nikolaos Krokos, Angeliki Chlorou, Ioannis Skandalos, Georgios Tsavdaris
pmc-13286624.description: Perforated necrotizing cholecystitis is a life-threatening complication of acute cholecystitis (AC), particularly in frail elderly patients, in whom atypical presentations may delay diagnosis. We report the case of an 89-year-old man with significant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal comorbidities who presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and a palpable right upper quadrant mass mimicking gallbladder hydrops at presentation.

pmc-13421113.title: Diffusion and clearance of ropivacaine after serratus anterior plane block by CT imaging: a prospective, single-arm trial
pmc-13421113.creator: Xin-lu Yang, Gao Wu, Fei Gao, Ting-ting Yan, Xian-ning Wu, Wei Gao, Shan Wang, Sheng Wang, Jia Yang

pmc-13630513.title: Distinct Roles of Directional and Positional Experience in De Novo Visuomotor Learning
pmc-13630513.creator: Tomoya Kawano, Shota Hagio
pmc-13630513.description: Humans can flexibly acquire entirely new sensorimotor mappings, a process known as de novo motor learning. A central challenge in de novo motor learning is that the learner must discover a viable solution from scratch within a highly redundant control space, without predefined task constraints.

pmc-13679565.title: Mononuclear Mg(ii) and Ca(ii) metallocarboxylates of N-phthaloyl-γ-aminobutyric acid: synthesis, characterization, ds-DNA binding, preliminary anticancer evaluation against MDA-MB-231 cells, and computational studies
pmc-13679565.creator: Naeem Abbas, Muhammad Arfan, Yasir Iqbal, Mudassir Iqbal, Naeem Ahmed, Mona G. Alharbi, Mansour K. Gatasheh
pmc-13679565.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study reports the synthesis of neurotransmitter-inspired, biolabile mononuclear Mg(ii)/(NY1) and Ca(ii)/(NY2) metallocarboxylates of N-phthaloyl-γ-aminobutyric acid ligand (NPGABA), motivated by the growing relevance of metallocarboxylates in addressing essential metal-ion deficiencies. Extensive spectral (i.e. IR, UV-vis, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, AAS, and ICP-AES) and analytical (SEM, micro-analysis and thermal gravimetric analysis) techniques were used to characterize and confirm the formation of the ligand and its metal carboxylate complexes.
